ablations.prompt: EXPLAIN INFLATION LIKE IM 10 NOT TOO LONG

runs.answer:
Inflation is when stuff gets more expensive over time.

Imagine a candy bar cost $1 when your parents were kids. Now it costs $2. The candy bar didn't get better. Money just got a little less powerful, so you need more of it to buy the same thing.

It happens because:
- **Lots of people want to buy things**, and sometimes there aren't quite enough things to go around, so sellers raise prices.
- **Making things costs more** (like wages, ingredients, or gas), so companies pass that cost on to you.
- **There's more money floating around**, so each dollar is worth a bit less.

A little inflation is normal and expected. A lot of it fast is a problem, because your savings buy less and less.

Inflation is when stuff gets more expensive over time.

Imagine a candy bar costs $1 today. Next year, it might cost $1.05. The candy bar is the same, but the money you have buys a little less of it. That's inflation.

It happens because prices of lots of things go up a bit each year, like food, toys, and gas. When that happens, your dollar can buy less than it used to.

A little bit of inflation is normal and expected. But if it goes up too fast, things get expensive quickly, and people have to work harder to buy the same stuff.
